Background In atrial fibrillation ( AF ), a more extensively fibrotic left atrium ( LA ) provides a substrate for arrhythmias and increases risk of relapse following ablation. Fibrocytes are bone marrow–derived circulating mesenchymal progenitors that have been identified in the atrium of patients with AF who have valvular diseases. The present study investigates the associations between circulating fibrocytes and LA fibrosis or the prevalence of recurrence after ablation in patients with persistent AF . Methods and Results We measured the proportion, differentiation, and migration of circulating fibrocytes from patients with persistent AF (n=40), those with paroxysmal AF (n=30), and sinus rhythm controls (n=30). LA low‐voltage (fibrosis) area was identified by an electroanatomic mapping system, and patients were followed up for 1 year after ablation. The relationship between circulating fibrocyte percentage and LA low‐voltage area or recurrence was assessed by multivariate regression analysis. Circulating fibrocyte percentage positively associated with LA low‐voltage area in the persistent AF group, and circulating fibrocyte (≥4.05%) was a significant predictor of 1‐year recurrence after ablation. Cultured fibrocytes exhibited enhanced potential of differentiation in the persistent AF group (67.58±1.54%) versus the paroxysmal AF group (56.67±1.52%) and sinus rhythm controls (48.43±1.79%). Furthermore, expression of fibroblast activation markers and cell migratory ability were also elevated in differentiated fibrocytes from patients with persistent AF . Transforming growth factor β1 and stromal cell–derived factor 1 were elevated in the plasma of patients with persistent AF and were shown to promote fibrocyte differentiation and migration, respectively. Conclusions In patients with persistent AF , increased circulating fibrocytes served as a marker of LA fibrosis and recurrence. atrial fibrillation atrial fibrosis fibrocyte differentiation biomarker Subject Categories Atrial Fibrillation Fibrosis Translational Studies National Nature Science Foundation of China 81201656 81630009 81500276 81570313 Chang Jiang Scholar Program of China source-schema-version-number 2.0 component-id jah33025 cover-date 20 March 2018 details-of-publishers-convertor Converter:WILEY_ML3GV2_TO_NLMPMC version:version=5.3.4 mode:remove_FC converted:10.04.2018 ( J Am Heart Assoc . 2018 ; 7 : e008083 DOI: 10.1161/JAHA.117.008083 .) 29535140 Clinical Perspective What Is New? Circulating fibrocytes were able to predict left atrial fibrosis status and atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after first‐time ablation in patients with persistent AF. Circulating fibrocytes from patients with persistent AF exhibited a hyperactivated status and had an enhanced capacity to differentiate into myofibroblasts. Transforming growth factor β1 and stromal cell–derived factor 1 were the causative mediators that promoted fibrocyte differentiation and migration, respectively. What Are the Clinical Implications? In patients with persistent AF, circulating fibrocytes could serve as a useful cellular marker both for the degree of left atrial fibrosis and the recurrence after single ablation. Inhibiting fibrocytes during AF progression might be useful as an adjuvant treatment to improve outcomes of catheter ablation for persistent AF. Introduction Atrial fibrillation (AF) is globally the most common arrhythmia contributing significantly to mortality and morbidity. 1 Large clinical trials have shown lack of significant benefits of using antiarrhythmic medications in the treatment of AF. 2 , 3 While catheter ablation has become the routine intervention for AF, recurrence rates remain high, ranging from 30% to 60% across reports. 4 , 5 Atrial structural remodeling together with fibrosis is an important mechanism for AF persistence. A more extensively fibrotic left atrium (LA) increases the rate of relapse after ablation. 6 , 7 To date, a reliable circulating marker that can predict atrial fibrosis and recurrence following ablation is limited. Resident cardiac fibroblasts are a primary source of collagen production during both homeostatic maintenance and the development of fibrosis. In addition, recent studies have implicated fibrocytes as another important cellular source of collagen, contributing to cardiac fibrosis. 8 Fibrocytes are circulating progenitor cells and are able to migrate to sites of tissue injury where they differentiate into fibroblasts and produce extracellular matrix proteins upon stimulation. 8 Fibrocytes express hematopoietic stem cell marker CD34, leukocyte marker CD45, and a variety of mesenchymal markers, including collagen I. 8 Recruitment of fibrocytes into tissue is associated with CD34 downregulation and α‐smooth muscle actin upregulation. 9 Fibrocytes are involved in various fibrotic disorders, including asthma, systemic sclerosis, and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 In addition, fibrocytes have been identified to contribute to myocardial infarction or heart failure–induced cardiac fibrosis in animal models. 14 , 15 , 16 Recently, fibrocytes were found in the atrium of patients with AF who had valvular heart diseases, 17 which prompted us to investigate the diagnostic value and functions of circulating fibrocytes in the setting of AF. In the present study, our hypothesis is that circulating fibrocytes are increased and activated in the setting of AF and could be an important indicator for LA fibrosis and AF recurrence following ablation.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the associations between circulating fibrocytes and left atrial (LA) fibrosis or the prevalence of recurrence after catheter ablation in patients with persistent and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF), compared to sinus rhythm controls. It examined fibrocyte proportion, differentiation, and migration, as well as gene expression of various molecular markers. The findings demonstrated that increased circulating fibrocytes positively correlate with LA fibrosis (low-voltage area) and are a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after ablation in persistent AF. Fibrocytes from persistent AF patients showed enhanced differentiation into myofibroblasts and elevated expression of pro-fibrotic and inflammatory markers, with TGF-β1 promoting differentiation and SDF-1 enhancing migration.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Catheter ablation was performed as a first-time or single procedure, predominantly for persistent AF. Specifics included radiofrequency energy applied with a power limit of 35 W and a maximal temperature of 45°C, applied until a voltage of <0.1 mV was achieved or for a maximum of 30 seconds per point. A single bolus of 100 IU/kg heparin was administered to maintain activated clotting time within 250-300 seconds. Oral antiplatelet/anticoagulant drugs were stopped 3 days before ablation and restored afterward, while antiarrhythmic drugs were stopped on the day of ablation and restored the next day for up to 2 months. Electroanatomic mapping systems were used to identify fibrotic (low-voltage) areas. Patients were followed up for 1 year post-ablation.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Proportion (percentage of total leukocytes), Differentiation potential, Migratory ability, Expression of fibroblast activation markers (CD45, CD34, Collagen I)

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Persistent AF: 3.24±0.51%; Paroxysmal AF: 2.58±0.16%; SR controls: 1.94±0.17%. Significantly higher in persistent AF compared to paroxysmal AF and SR controls (P<0.05). Percentage positively associated with LA low-voltage area. A percentage ≥4.05% (62% sensitivity, 96% specificity) was a significant predictor of 1-year recurrence after single ablation in persistent AF (P=0.05). A percentage ≥4.10% was a significant predictor for all AF patients. Cultured fibrocytes from persistent AF showed enhanced differentiation potential (67.58±1.54%) versus paroxysmal AF (56.67±1.52%) and SR controls (48.43±1.79%). Expression of fibroblast activation markers and cell migratory ability were elevated in differentiated fibrocytes from persistent AF.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Bone marrow-derived circulating mesenchymal progenitors that differentiate into myofibroblasts, producing extracellular matrix proteins and inflammatory mediators, thereby contributing to cardiac fibrosis and remodeling.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Persistent and Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (AF), associated with LA fibrosis and post-catheter ablation recurrence.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A useful cellular marker for assessing the degree of LA fibrosis and predicting 1-year recurrence after single ablation, particularly in persistent AF patients, and indicates a hyperactivated status with enhanced capacity to differentiate into myofibroblasts.

analyzed_biomarkers.activity_type: Protein Level (concentration); Gene Transcript (mRNA); Differentiation Promotion

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma levels significantly elevated in persistent AF. Gene expression significantly upregulated in differentiated fibrocytes from persistent AF compared to SR controls and paroxysmal AF groups. Recombinant TGF-β1 promoted differentiation of SR control-derived fibrocytes into fibroblasts as compared with that cultured in medium alone.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A key cytokine and major driver of fibrosis, promoting cell growth, extracellular matrix production, and particularly the differentiation of fibrocytes into myofibroblasts via activating Smad2/3 and stress-activated protein kinase/c-Jun N-terminal kinase pathways.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Persistent Atrial Fibrillation (AF); in vitro regulation of fibrocyte differentiation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A causative mediator of fibrocyte differentiation and a key contributor to LA fibrosis and AF recurrence; elevated systemic levels indicate a heightened pro-fibrotic environment in persistent AF. Targeting TGF-β1/TGF-βR1 may be a useful treatment to prevent AF progression or improve ablation outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Plasma levels significantly elevated in persistent AF compared to paroxysmal AF and SR controls, and restored after cardioversion. Recombinant SDF-1 markedly enhanced migratory ability of SR control-derived fibrocytes compared with vehicle control, but had less ability to promote differentiation compared to TGF-β1.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: A chemokine and ligand for CXCR4 that regulates mobilization and migration of stem cells, including fibrocytes, playing a predominant role in promoting fibrocyte chemotaxis and trafficking.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Persistent Atrial Fibrillation (AF); in vitro regulation of fibrocyte migration and differentiation.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: A causative mediator of fibrocyte migration that contributes to LA fibrosis and AF recurrence. Elevated systemic levels in persistent AF suggest its role in recruiting fibrocytes to fibrotic areas, and targeting SDF-1/CXCR4 may be useful for preventing AF progression or improving ablation outcomes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: The number of spindle-shaped cells per field was markedly increased in the persistent AF group compared with the paroxysmal AF group or SR control group.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Fibrocytes differentiated into myofibroblast-like cells, indicating enhanced fibrotic potential.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: In vitro culture of leukocytes derived from Persistent AF, Paroxysmal AF, and SR patients.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an enhanced ability of fibrocytes from persistent AF patients to differentiate into myofibroblasts, suggesting a higher intrinsic fibrotic tendency associated with persistent AF.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased proportion of differentiated fibrocytes (CD45+/collagen I+) in patients with persistent AF (67.58±1.54%) compared with those with paroxysmal AF (56.67±1.52%) and SR controls (48.43±1.79%).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Identifies fibrocytes that have undergone differentiation towards a myofibroblast-like phenotype, indicating fibrotic activity.

analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates a higher percentage of fibrocytes with myofibroblast characteristics in persistent AF patients, suggesting active fibrotic processes.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Content was higher at mRNA and protein levels in differentiated fibrocytes from AF patients compared to the paroxysmal AF group and SR controls, indicating a hyperactivated status.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Expression levels were significantly upregulated in the persistent AF group relative to SR control and paroxysmal AF groups.
